title: Automated Tools: Your First Line of Defence 🛡️
description: Master axe DevTools, Lighthouse, WAVE, and browser extensions to catch common issues instantly.

slides.title: Your Accessibility Toolkit 🧰
slides.content:
Browser extensions and command‑line tools can quickly scan for violations. Top picks:

- **axe DevTools** (Chrome/Firefox) – the industry standard, used in Lighthouse.
- **WAVE** (WebAIM) – visual overlays, contrast checker, structural analysis.
- **Lighthouse** (built into Chrome DevTools) – scores performance, SEO, and accessibility.
- **Microsoft Accessibility Insights** – advanced manual testing helper.
- **HTML_CodeSniffer** – bookmarklet for quick checks.

All are free and essential.

quizData.question: Which automated tool is integrated into Chrome DevTools and provides an accessibility score?
quizData.explanation: Lighthouse includes an accessibility audit powered by axe‑core.

slides.title: axe DevTools in Action ⚙️
slides.content:
Install the extension, open DevTools → axe tab, and click 'Scan all of my page'. Results are categorized by impact:

- **Critical**: missing labels, buttons without text.
- **Serious**: low contrast, missing document language.
- **Moderate**: skipped heading levels.
- **Minor**: things to review.

Each issue links to detailed documentation. Use it while developing – scan every new component.

quizData.question: What does axe DevTools test that a human might miss?

options.text: Whether a video has accurate captions
If an input has an associated label
If a page is easy to understand

quizData.explanation: axe checks for programmatic associations; caption accuracy requires human judgment.

slides.title: Lighthouse: Accessibility Score 🌟
slides.content:
Lighthouse generates a report with a 0‑100 score. It tests about 40% of WCAG criteria automatically. It's great for:

- Quick health checks.
- Performance + a11y in one view.
- CI integration (Lighthouse CI).

But a score of 100 does not mean perfectly accessible – it only means no automated issues were found.

slides.title: WAVE: Visual Feedback 🟨
slides.content:
WAVE adds icons and indents to your page:

- Red boxes = errors.
- Yellow boxes = alerts.
- Green boxes = features (like ARIA, headings).

It's excellent for seeing the structure at a glance and spotting missing headings, empty links, and contrast issues.

quizData.question: What does WAVE use to indicate an error?
quizData.explanation: WAVE overlays icons directly on the page to mark issues.

slides.title: Command‑Line & CI Tools 🖥️
slides.content:
For automated pipelines:

- **axe‑core** (npm) – use with Playwright, Cypress, Jest.
- **pa11y** – simple CLI, outputs JSON.
- **Lighthouse CI** – sets score budgets, blocks PRs if score drops.

Run these on every commit to prevent regressions.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Don't stop at the scan
Automated tools are a starting point. Always follow up with manual testing.
